title: StudyBuddy
description: An accessible teaching assistant grounded in the learner’s own PDFs.; Stakeholder overview

title: StudyBuddy connects source material with active learning
description: Private classrooms built from uploaded PDFs; Teaching, practice, and adaptive examinations in one workflow; Answers linked to verified source evidence; Accessibility controls built into the learning experience

title: Stakeholder overview
description: The learning need and product approach; The student journey and core features; Grounding, accessibility, and data boundaries; Current limitations and a proposed pilot

title: Students need more than a place to read their notes
description: Reading alone does not show what a student understands; Generic chat answers may go beyond assigned material; Learners need explanations, practice, and feedback; Access needs should not prevent participation

title: One classroom defines what the tutor can teach
description: Upload notes, textbook chapters, or slides as PDFs; Each classroom has a fixed set of source documents; The tutor uses that classroom’s source map; No web search or cross-classroom facts are added

title: The student journey follows a repeatable learning loop
description: Set learning preferences; Create a classroom and upload PDFs; Review document coverage before learning; Learn, practise, test, and review progress

title: Personalization changes presentation, not source facts
description: Capture study level, goals, pace, and explanation style; Adjust session length and vocabulary support; Record confidence, interests, and optional access needs; Preferences can be updated as the learner’s needs change

title: PDF analysis combines visual content with extracted text
description: Render pages so diagrams and tables can be examined; Combine Gemini vision analysis with the PDF text layer; Build concepts linked to text, figure, and table evidence; Show page coverage and flag verification gaps

title: Teaching checks understanding rather than only answering questions
description: Use diagnostics to identify the learner’s starting point; Explain concepts using classroom evidence; Ask the student to explain the idea back; Provide feedback linked to the original source

title: Practice makes assistance visible
description: Free recall, quick quizzes, figure labels, and application tasks; Quick quizzes include multiple-choice and short-answer questions; Page and quotation hints support students who need help; Hint use is tracked so assisted attempts remain distinguishable

title: Adaptive examinations reveal concepts that need more work
description: Questions adjust in difficulty as the student responds; Citations appear after an answer, not before; Feedback connects results to classroom concepts; Results feed the learner’s progress view

title: Progress is based on the student’s recorded attempts
description: Concept-level mastery shows where to focus; Six learning dimensions summarize performance; Review reminders identify concepts to revisit; Recent attempts and recommended next steps support planning

title: Accessibility is part of the core interface
description: Keyboard-first navigation and a skip-to-content link; Readable typography and a large-text setting; High-contrast and reduced-motion settings; Screen-reader labels and a text table alongside the progress chart; Formal accessibility conformance has not yet been established

title: Source grounding makes answers inspectable
description: Verify citation quotations against stored source evidence; Let students open the cited PDF page; Show original figures and tables rather than AI replacements; Decline questions outside the classroom’s evidence; Grounding reduces unsupported answers; it does not guarantee correctness

title: Private classrooms separate each learner’s material
description: Signed-in access and classroom ownership checks; Original PDFs stored in private object storage; PostgreSQL stores profiles, classroom metadata, and learning attempts; Gemini processes page content and learning requests; Retention, consent, and institutional compliance require review before rollout

title: Verification and latency remain important product constraints
description: Unverified pages can block teaching, practice, and exams; Persistent page jobs support recovery after interruptions; Failed pages can be retried while verified evidence is retained; PDF complexity and AI service limits affect waiting time; No published latency target or learning-outcome evidence is claimed

title: A focused pilot can test value before wider adoption
description: Use representative text-heavy, scanned, and diagram-rich PDFs; Evaluate grounded-answer accuracy and page-verification failures; Test keyboard and assistive-technology journeys with learners; Measure processing time, response latency, completion, and cost; Review learning outcomes with educators

title: Stakeholder discussion and next steps
description: Agree the first learner group and subject area; Nominate educators to validate source-grounded responses; Set accessibility, privacy, reliability, and cost acceptance criteria; Decide whether to proceed with a limited pilot; Defer wider rollout until those criteria are met
